articles.title: Beetaloo Energy (ASX:BTL) Quarterly Activities Report: Advances Carpentaria Pilot Project Towards Q4 2026 Commissioning
articles.description: Beetaloo Energy Australia Limited (ASX:BTL) (OTCMKTS:EEGUF) progressed construction of its Carpentaria Gas Plant during the quarter ended 30 September 2026, with commissioning and first pilot gas sales anticipated in Q4 2026. The Company also completed the Carpentaria-5H IP30 flow test and acquisition of the Birdum Creek 2D Seismic Survey. Carpentaria Pilot Project and Western Beetaloo Mechanical work on the Carpentaria Gas Plant was largely complete, with the focus on completing the instrumentation and electrical work before commissioning. The Carpentaria Pilot Project was tracking on schedule and budget for commissioning in Q4 2026. On 13 July 2026, Beetaloo Energy announced completion of the Carpentaria-5H IP30 flow test. The well achieved a peak flow rate exceeding 14 TJ/day, an average rate of 6.9 TJ/day over the 30-day test period and an exit rate of 6.7 TJ/day. Following testing, Carpentaria-5H was shut in pending connection to the Carpentaria Gas Plant alongside Carpentaria-2H and Carpentaria-3H. Acquisition of the 236-kilometre Birdum Creek 2D Seismic Survey across EP167 and EP168 was completed by the end of July. The survey covers the Western Beetaloo gas discovery area and is designed to improve subsurface characterisation, refine structural interpretation and inform the placement of future horizontal wells. Beetaloo Digital On 22 July 2026, the Company announced the launch of Beetaloo Digital, a wholly owned subsidiary established to progress a proposed vertically integrated gas-to-power and data centre development in the Northern Territory. The Northern Territory Government granted the Company exclusivity over approximately 185 hectares of contiguous land at Weddell, south-east of Darwin, enabling concept and pre-FEED studies and discussions with prospective consortium partners. Beetaloo Energy announced a non-binding Memorandum of Understanding with Halliburton on 30 July 2026 to support assessment of the upstream gas resource underpinning Beetaloo Digital. On 24 August 2026, the Company announced a non-binding Memorandum of Understanding with Australian Gas Infrastructure Group to assess gas transportation and associated infrastructure. The work includes preliminary assessment of an approximately 750-kilometre pipeline from the Carpentaria Gas Project towards future demand centres in the Darwin area, together with gas processing and associated facilities. Financial Position and Funding In its quarterly commentary, the Company reported total available liquidity of $113.2 million, comprising cash of $51.7 million and undrawn amounts of $17.6 million under the Research and Development Facility, $42.5 million under the Midstream Facility and $1.5 million under the Performance Bond Facility. All facilities are held with Macquarie Bank. The Company reported in its quarterly commentary that, on 28 September 2026, it received its FY2025 Research and Development Tax Incentive refund of approximately $19.1 million, together with $0.3 million in interest. In accordance with the terms of its Macquarie Research and Development Facility, the Company intends to fully repay the outstanding loan balance of approximately $12.4 million within 30 days of receipt of the refund. No drawdowns were made under the Company's $30 million Research and Development Credit Facility or $45 million Midstream Infrastructure Facility during the quarter. Capitalised exploration expenditure totalled $20,550,816, comprising $17,880,723 for the Carpentaria Pilot Project and $2,670,093 for the Birdum Creek 2D Seismic Survey. Expensed exploration expenditure totalled $1,608,990. The Company continued to provide funding to Territory Sands under the loan agreement supporting development of the proposed Forest Hill South frac sand operation. Total loan drawdowns amounted to approximately $7.4 million at 30 September 2026. Community Engagement Beetaloo Energy supported the Malandarri Festival in Borroloola, celebrating the culture, traditions and creativity of the Gulf region. Bringing local communities together through music, dance, art and cultural activities, the festival provides an opportunity to celebrate First Nations culture and strengthen community connections. The Company's support reflects its ongoing commitment to building positive relationships with communities across the Northern Territory and contributing to initiatives that celebrate local culture and community wellbeing. Beetaloo Energy also sponsored the Top End Bull Spectacular, which celebrates the Northern Territory's agricultural heritage and rodeo traditions. The event brings together competitors, families and spectators from across the region, providing an opportunity to showcase local talent and strengthen community connections. The sponsorship reinforces the Company's commitment to supporting grassroots initiatives and contributing to the vibrant communities of the Northern Territory. *To view the Quarterly Report, please visit: https://abnnewswire.net/lnk/1037V8SW Editorial Note: This media release has been independently prepared by ABN Newswire editorial staff based on Beetaloo Energy's Quarterly Report. It is intended as an editorial summary of information disclosed in that report and should be read in conjunction with Beetaloo Energy's full ASX announcement. All financial, operational and post-reporting-period information in this editorial has been sourced from the Company's report. Brookfield, NextEra To Build $100 Billion AI Hub On Cold War Nuclear Site
articles.description: Brookfield, NextEra To Build $100 Billion AI Hub On Cold War Nuclear Site Authored by Alex Kimani via OilPrice, The U.S. Department of Energy (DoE) has announced a landmark $100-billion private investment to turn the former uranium enrichment site in Western Kentucky into the new Paducah American Energy Hub, marking one of the largest economic development projects in Kentucky's history. Led by U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright, the initiative will bring together a private-sector coalition to build a massive artificial intelligence and high-performance computing (HPC) innovation campus powered by new energy infrastructure. The phased buildout is targeted for 2032, and is expected to create roughly 8,000 construction jobs and 600 permanent operations jobs. Brookfield Asset Management (NYSE:BAM) has been selected to build the 1.8-gigawatt (GW) AI and HPC data center campus while NextEra Energy (NYSE:NEE) will develop 2 GW of natural gas-fired generation coupled with 2.6 GW of battery energy storage. The project is designed to operate on dedicated power supplies capable of feeding excess energy back to the regional grid to avoid raising utility bills for local families and businesses. The campus will also deploy a modern closed-loop cooling system to continuously recirculate water and minimize external consumption. The project leaders emphasize that this design is vastly more resource-efficient compared to the site's previous tenant, the Cold War-era Paducah Gaseous Diffusion Plant, which was originally designed to pull up to 30 million gallons of water per day from the Ohio River. Still, the Paducah project comes at a time when the market is souring on heavy AI infrastructure spending. Last year, Trump, alongside Oracle's Larry Ellison, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and SoftBank CEO Masayoshi Son, unveiled Stargate, a private-sector joint venture intended to invest up to $500 billion over four years to build hyper-scale AI data centers and energy infrastructure across the United States. Billed by Trump as the "largest AI infrastructure project in history," Stargate is designed to secure American dominance in AI over foreign competitors like China. Oracle serves as the core cloud and infrastructure provider for the venture. Initial development of the project began in Abilene, Texas, consisting of multiple 500,000-square-foot data center buildings to house the immense computing power needed for next-generation AI models. Unfortunately, the ambitious AI infrastructure project found itself on the ropes just months after its grand launch. Back in January, Business Insider reported that JPMorgan Chase was having trouble syndicating the $38 billion in construction debt it underwrote for the Stargate AI data center initiative as institutional investors grow increasingly cautious regarding concentrated tech sector exposure. Banks spent more than six months attempting to distribute the multi-billion-dollar debt packages for the Stargate campuses located in Texas and Wisconsin; however, buyers appeared uninterested in taking on massive piles of debt tied heavily to single-tenant AI operations. Oracle leases the facilities, and S&P cut Oracle in July to BBB-, one notch above junk, over its data center spending. Investors demanded a higher return to hold the debt, and the banks had to sell it at a discount. In April, OpenAI officially paused its Stargate UK data center project, citing high industrial electricity prices and regulatory uncertainty. Stargate UK was planned in partnership with hardware firms Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) and Nscale, aiming to deploy thousands of advanced AI chips (starting with 8,000 GPUs and scaling up to 31,000) across sites in North-East England, including Cobalt Park near Newcastle and Blyth. Whereas OpenAI did not cancel the project outright, the AI giant says it will only resume development only when the "right conditions" allow for long-term infrastructure investment. The pause dealt a major blow to UK infrastructure partner Nscale (founded by Josh Payne), which had been scaling up operations and weighing a potential stock market IPO, as well as Britain's push to emerge as a sovereign AI superpower. The UK pause is the second blow to OpenAI's planned capacity in a month. Last month, Bloomberg reported that Oracle's pivotal $18-billion Project Jupiter, a massive 1,400-acre data center campus in New Mexico critical to supporting the broader AI infrastructure goals, has stalled. Oracle issued a force majeure notice to lender Blue Owl Capital regarding the 2.45-gigawatt hyperscale data center in southern New Mexico after the tech giant failed to secure vital state and federal land-use permits for a planned natural gas plant. Instead, Oracle announced plans to shift over to solid oxide fuel cells (SOFCs), an experimental stopgap that has never been deployed on a scale this large. Public resistance to data centers has been growing rapidly across the United States, Europe and Asia as communities push back against the massive environmental and economic footprint of AI infrastructure. A recent Gallup poll shows that roughly 71% of Americans oppose the construction of AI data centers in their localities. Pushback in the U.S. has resulted in projects worth over $130 billion blocked or delayed, with reports indicating more than 500 active data center bans or moratoriums have popped up nationwide. Tyler Durden Mon, 10/19/2026 - 19:15

articles.title: US stocks rebound while Europe falls on unrest
articles.description: The Nasdaq rose more than 1 percent on Monday as tech shares rebounded ahead of a big week for AI-related earnings, while European stocks and the euro fell as unrest in France added to concerns about the country's fiscal outlook. French bonds and Paris-listed stocks also fell as the widespread protests across France underscored the difficulties the government faces in reducing its large deficit. France's central government asked some local authorities to impose curfews as it faced pressure over security failings on Monday, after looting stemming from the protests. Tech stocks on Wall Street recovered some ground after a bruising week, with an index of semiconductors up 1.6 percent. On Friday, the index sank in its eighth straight day of declines, its longest losing streak since 2008. With results due from Meta on Wednesday, and results from Tesla and chipmakers Lam Research and Texas Instruments also due this week, investors will be watching for signs that massive AI spending ultimately pays off. "Investors are buying the correction dip that we had," said Peter Cardillo, chief market economist at Spartan Capital Securities in New York. "The market is now going to go through a very critical test over the next two weeks. We have some big-name earnings coming out," he said. "In terms of technology, the test of whether or not the spending on AI... will be met with satisfaction is going to be critical." The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 36 points, or 0.1 percent, to 51,966, the S&P 500 rose 31 points, or 0.4 percent, to 7,690 and the Nasdaq Composite rose 290 points, or 1.1 percent, to 26,430. Meta is one of five AI hyperscalers expected to increase combined capital expenditure to about US$1.2 trillion next year, according to Goldman Sachs. Results from SpaceX are also due on Tuesday. Overall, US earnings are still expected to rise about 30 percent, largely driven by growth in the technology sector. US Treasury yields rose on Monday, with the benchmark 10-year Treasury yield coming off its biggest weekly drop in seven months, as concerns about the impact of higher interest rates on AI stocks abated. The yield on the benchmark US 10-year Treasury note was up 4.2 basis points at 5.14 percent. The pan-European STOXX 600 index fell 0.8 percent, while France's blue-chip CAC 40 index dropped 1.1 percent. France's 10-year yield earlier was up 13 basis points to 4.9 percent while the German 10-year yield, the benchmark for the euro zone, was also higher. (Reuters) Edited by Cecil Wong
